children: Australia on Thursday relaxed slightly a proposed rule that would have forced energy exporters to reserve a fixed 20% of natural gas for its east coast market, instead requiring them to reserve up to a fifth of production.

Energy Minister Chris Bowen said exporters could provide up to 200 additional petajoules of gas per year, more than enough to avoid the possible shortfalls of up to 140 petajoules forecast by the country's energy market operator.
The proposed policy will ensure "gas is more affordable and the domestic market is always modestly oversupplied," Bowen said in a statement.

"The scheme ensures domestic customers can buy from a larger pool of gas, reducing the risk of tight market conditions driving price spikes, promoting long-term contracting and shielding them from global volatility," he said.

The changes come four months after the centre-left Labor government proposed a hard 20% gas reservation scheme for the country's east coast market in May. In December, the government had proposed a plan to reserve between 15% and 25% of gas.
Three liquefied natural gas (LNG) export projects on the east coast operated by Origin Energy
will be affected by the reservation scheme, though existing contracts will be exempt.
Shares in Santos, which operates the Gladstone LNG project in Queensland, and Origin Energy, which leads rival export consortium Australia Pacific LNG, were slightly higher in early morning trade.

Australia is one of the world's largest LNG exporters and ships more gas overseas than it consumes domestically. However, most of the country's gas reserves are located in its northwest region, far from the more populous southeast, where demand is concentrated.
The state of Western Australia already has its own reservation scheme that requires offshore export projects to divert 15% of their gas output to the local market.

Bowen also said the scheme's start date would be pushed back by six months "to align with industry contracting cycles," meaning LNG exporters would not need to meet their supply commitments until January 1, 2028.

The government on Thursday released a draft of the policy, seeking feedback until September 24, after receiving more than 140 submissions from gas producers and exporters, retailers, large industrial users and trade partners during the policy's preliminary planning phase.
The bill is expected to be introduced to parliament later this year.
